Rename normalizeInvoiceReference to canonicalizeInvoiceReference in its declaration and all calls. Make no other change. Return the complete edited document only, without explanation. Do not omit unchanged lines.

// Reference formatting for a fictional billing application.
// The parser deliberately keeps the original input for diagnostics.
const PREFIX = "INV";
const DIGITS = /^\d{6}$/;

export function normalizeInvoiceReference(input) {
  if (typeof input !== "string") {
    return { ok: false, reason: "not-a-string", original: input };
  }
  const trimmed = input.trim();
  const pieces = trimmed.split("-");
  if (pieces.length !== 2 || pieces[0].toUpperCase() !== PREFIX) {
    return { ok: false, reason: "invalid-prefix", original: input };
  }
  if (!DIGITS.test(pieces[1])) {
    return { ok: false, reason: "invalid-number", original: input };
  }
  return { ok: true, value: `${PREFIX}-${pieces[1]}`, original: input };
}

export function classifyReferences(values) {
  const accepted = [];
  const rejected = [];
  for (const value of values) {
    const result = normalizeInvoiceReference(value);
    if (result.ok) {
      accepted.push(result.value);
    } else {
      rejected.push({ value, reason: result.reason });
    }
  }
  return { accepted, rejected };
}

export function uniqueReferences(values) {
  const seen = new Set();
  for (const value of values) {
    const result = normalizeInvoiceReference(value);
    if (result.ok) seen.add(result.value);
  }
  return Array.from(seen).sort();
}

export const examples = [
  "inv-000041",
  " INV-000042 ",
  "INV-12",
  "receipt-000043",
];<|im_end|>

# Harbor recovery runbook

This fictional runbook describes a rehearsal in a disposable environment. The
rehearsal owner records each observation in the shared worksheet before moving
to the next step. A successful rehearsal includes a verified rollback, not only
a successful restoration.

## Preparation

1. Confirm the rehearsal environment name and the maintenance window.
2. Record the current application version and configuration revision.
3. Check that the most recent backup has completed its integrity check.
4. Save the expected record count and a small set of representative identifiers.
5. Assign one person to operate the service and another to record observations.

## Procedure

Use the [restoration guide](https://example.test/operations/restore-v1) for the
command sequence. Copy the backup into a fresh workspace and leave the source
artifact unchanged. Start the restored service with outgoing integrations
disabled. Verify the health endpoint, then compare record counts and selected
identifiers with the preparation worksheet.

Run the read-only acceptance queries before enabling any scheduled job. Record
the elapsed time for each phase separately: download, integrity verification,
restoration, startup and acceptance checks. If a check fails, retain the logs
and stop the rehearsal at that point.

## Rollback and cleanup

Return traffic to the original rehearsal instance and confirm its health.
Remove only the temporary workspace created for this run. Preserve the source
backup, the worksheet and the logs until the review is complete. List any
manual step that was missing from the documented procedure.

## Review

The owner writes a short follow-up describing the first failed check, any
unexpected wait and the smallest documentation change that would have helped.
A reviewer confirms that the restored data and the rollback were both checked.

Fictional document-editing exercise: shared equipment arrangement

1. Purpose. The participants share the equipment listed in the inventory for
scheduled demonstrations and internal training. This arrangement does not
transfer ownership of the equipment or authorize its use outside the agreed
locations.

2. Scheduling. Each participant records a requested session in the calendar.
A confirmed session states its start time, end time, location and responsible
operator. The operator checks the inventory before use and reports any missing
item to the coordinator.

3. Care. Participants keep the equipment clean, follow the supplied operating
instructions and return accessories to their labelled containers. Consumable
items are recorded separately so that the inventory remains useful between
sessions.

4. Changes. A participant requesting a change to a confirmed session gives the
coordinator at least ten business days of written notice. The coordinator
records the request, consults any affected participant and confirms the revised
schedule in writing. An unanswered request does not change the calendar.

5. Records. The coordinator retains the inventory, confirmed schedule and
reported incidents in the shared folder. Each incident record states what was
observed, when it was observed and which item was involved, without assigning
fault before the review.

6. Review. The participants review this arrangement at the end of the training
season. Any agreed revision is dated and circulated together with a copy of
the previous version. All sections outside the agreed revision remain intact.
